sources.title: Thylacoleo carnifex
sources.author: Anne Musser / Australian Museum
sources.location: Identification; Feeding and diet; Specimen in our collection
sources.supports: Short broad skull, slicing premolars, specialized incisors and enlarged fore-thumb claw. Museum skull display combines AM F.4661 with AM F.109727 and digitally estimated missing parts.
sources.limits: Do not turn the mixed skull display into a single complete specimen or repeat speculative feeding behavior as observation. Fossil Record widget and body text differ in epoch labels; use the species-level Pleistocene context supported by the primary studies.
sources.rights: Australian Museum page and artwork retain their stated rights; consulted, not embedded or used as model texture.
sources.incorporation: No image, mesh or scan incorporated.

sources.title: New skeletal material sheds light on the palaeobiology of the Pleistocene marsupial carnivore, Thylacoleo carnifex
sources.author: Roderick T. Wells and Aaron B. Camens
sources.location: Figures 1, 2 and 11; axial skeleton and discussion
sources.supports: Named Nullarbor and Naracoorte specimens, robust caudal base, comparatively rigid lumbar region and complete-body reconstruction.
sources.limits: Figure 11 includes an interpreted body outline. Posture and locomotion are hypotheses; avoid copying it as an exact living silhouette or photographic record.
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0, Wells and Camens (2018). Figure 1 photographs credited to Clay Bryce (A) and S. Bourne (B,C).
sources.incorporation: Figures consulted only; no reference image pixels or mesh embedded in public delivery.

sources.title: Pedal morphology of the marsupial lion Thylacoleo carnifex (Diprotodontia: Thylacoleonidae) from the Pleistocene of Australia
sources.author: Roderick T. Wells, Peter F. Murray and Steven J. Bourne
sources.location: Description and comparison of pes, pp. 1336-1339; SAM P43220 and SAM P43221
sources.supports: Plantigrade hindfoot, close digits II-III, slender clawed digits II-V and divergent hallux.
sources.limits: The hallux tip was not preserved; authors infer a blunt clawless form. Do not claim a complete observed hallux or fully opposable koala-like hind thumb.
sources.rights: Copyright 2009 Society of Vertebrate Paleontology; consulted through Western Australian Museum library copy, not embedded.
sources.incorporation: No PDF or figure included in public delivery.

sources.title: Warrnambool Thylacoleo moving across a dune
sources.author: Flinders University, Virtual Australian Museum of Palaeontology
sources.supports: Five-digit forepaw impression including the large semi-opposable thumb, Late Pleistocene Bridgewater Formation.
sources.limits: Trackway description supports digit arrangement, not exact living claw sheath or foot-pad dimensions.
sources.rights: Flinders University; consulted only, no images or scan incorporated.
sources.incorporation: No external model, texture or image included.
